pr.body: Updated api.py to validate limit as an integer from 1 to 100 (default 20), paginate in ascending ID order, and return {items, next_cursor}; malformed limits/cursors return HTTP-shaped 400 {error}. Opaque cursor tokens are random and resolved through an in-process issued-token map. Updated README.md and test_api.py, including full page traversal, boundary/error validation, and 5,000-digit limit regression coverage. python3 -m unittest passed (7 tests); git diff --check passed. Assumption: cursor registry is process-local, matching this in-memory service; cursors do not survive restarts or cross worker processes, and issued tokens accumulate during process lifetime.
pr.summary: GET /items now returns ordered pages with validated limits and opaque cursors. Before: all items returned at once; now: clients can continue via next_cursor until the final null cursor.

pr.body: Implemented GET /items cursor pages and documented the API in README.md. Limit parsing bounds input length before integer conversion, including 5,000-digit values. Cursors encode the last ID and authenticate it with HMAC, avoiding process-local state and unbounded token storage. Tests cover ordered traversal, invalid cursors, limits, and the huge-limit regression. `python3 -m unittest` passed all 7 tests; `git diff --check` passed. Assumption: service instances share the code's cursor secret; rotating it invalidates outstanding cursors. Client companion change is handled in the sibling inventory-client repository.
pr.summary: Added opaque cursor pagination to GET /items with ascending ID order. Before: requests returned only the first page and oversized limits could fail conversion; now: callers can follow stateless cursors, invalid input returns 400, and the 1..100 limit is validated safely.
pr.title: Implement cursor pagination in inventory API

risk.why: Contained behavior change to GET /items, README, and tests. Stateless authenticated cursors and limit validation are covered by passing tests. Medium reflects the public API behavior change. Embedded cursor secret requires compatible deployments and invalidates outstanding cursors on rotation.
